name: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
blurb: Sockeye salmon, brown bears and wolves beneath active volcanoes.

tip.title: Remove the sockeye run
tip.text: Sockeye feed bears, wolves, gulls and ravens. Set Sockeye salmon to -100% and watch the bears and the wolf pack that depends on salmon.

nodes.desc: Long summer days power a short growing season for tundra, willow and lake algae; winters are dark and cold.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and spawned-out salmon, returning nutrients to soil and water.
Grass-like plants of wet meadows and salt marshes. Sedges are a spring staple for brown bears, and the park notes salt marshes are key bear feeding areas.
A shrub willow of tundra and river flats. Willow twigs and buds feed moose, hares and ptarmigan.
A low berry shrub of tundra and bogs. Its leaves and berries are eaten by caribou, ptarmigan and bears.
Drifting microscopic algae in lakes that feed zooplankton. General ecological knowledge.
Tundra herds that eat sedges, shrubs and lichens. The park herds have fallen from about 200,000 to 30,000 for reasons not fully known.
Large browser of willow and other shrubs in river valleys and boreal forest. Prey of wolves and bears.
Small rodent of wet meadows that eats sedges and grasses. Prey for stoats, gulls, ravens and bears.
Burrowing hibernator of tundra slopes. Brown bears are known to dig out and catch it.
Grouse of tundra and shrub thickets that eats willow buds and berries. Preyed on by wolves, bears and stoats.
Browser of willow twigs in boreal thickets. Main prey of Canada lynx and also eaten by wolves.
Returns from the sea to spawn in park lakes and streams; the Kvichak is described as the most productive sockeye watershed. Adults die after spawning.
Small weasel that hunts voles, shrews, hares and ptarmigan under snow and over tundra.
Boreal cat that depends heavily on snowshoe hares.
Omnivorous scavenger that picks over carcasses, including bear-left salmon and winter-killed game, and takes small animals.
Gathers on the coast to feed on spawning salmon and salt-marsh sedges; also eats berries, carrion and small and large prey.
Hunts caribou, moose and hares. A Lake Clark pack is documented as the only salmon-dependent wolf pack in the world.

story: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve in southwest Alaska, about 100 miles from Anchorage, protects coastal rainforest, alpine tundra, glaciers, glacial lakes and two volcanoes, Redoubt and Iliamna. Its streams and lakes are vital to the Bristol Bay salmon fishery. No roads lead to it.
matters: Sockeye salmon play a major role in the ecosystem and local economy. Large populations of brown bears feed on spawning salmon in the Kijik River and at Silver Salmon Creek.
